title: Dinosaur Valley RV Park

services.name: RV Sites
services.desc: Every RV site at Dinosaur Valley RV Park includes full hookups with 30 amp and 50 amp service, water, and on‑site sewer. All sites are 80‑foot pull‑throughs, giving you plenty of room for big rigs, tow vehicles, and easy arrival and departure. Dinosaur Valley RV Park is located on the Paluxy River in Glen Rose, Texas, next to Dinosaur Valley State Park. All RV sites are within walking distance of the river, two swimming pools, an adult-only hot tub, and the trailhead into the state park. Fossil Rim Wildlife Center and downtown Glen Rose are a short drive from the park. Rates vary by date and availability. Select your dates and click Check Availability to view current pricing. services.name: The Campground
services.desc: Dinosaur Valley RV Park offers family-friendly activities every season. Guests enjoy two swimming pools, Paluxy River access for wading and tubing, hiking trails into Dinosaur Valley State Park, a playground with a frontier-style fort, barnyard animals, a bike trail, RC car track, and golf cart rentals. Seasonal events include chili cookoffs, holiday celebrations, and outdoor movie nights. Explore our full list of park amenities or browse nearby area attractions to plan your visit. services.name: Cabin stay
services.desc: Cabins for Our Glampers. Dinosaur Valley RV Park cabins are located on the Paluxy River in Glen Rose, Texas, directly adjacent to Dinosaur Valley State Park. Guests staying in cabins have full access to the park's two swimming pools, adult-only hot tub, river frontage, and hiking trails. Fossil Rim Wildlife Center, the Creation Evidence Museum, and historic downtown Glen Rose are all just minutes away. Enjoy the comfort of our brand‑new, climate‑controlled cabins, available in two layouts: Each cabin features a fully furnished living room and kitchen, private bedroom(s), and a cozy sleeping loft. blurb: Welcome to Dinosaur Valley RV Park - your family’s basecamp for adventure along the beautiful Paluxy River. Our park sits on land rich with history, from ancient dinosaur tracks to the Native American tribes who later lived throughout this region. Today, we honor that heritage with a nostalgic frontier‑style atmosphere paired with the modern comforts travelers expect.
